title: Precision weights kept mean abundance response signs in six bird drought samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether precision weights change the sign of the mean bird abundance response to drought. We used 179 records and 151 study-species units in six study samples from a 2024 public release. Four means were negative and two were positive with both equal record weights and inverse reported variance weights. Absolute mean size changes ranged from a 24 percent reduction to a 131 percent increase. Added variance and equal-species checks kept all signs. One-species omissions reversed the small positive Spanish result. Four samples had group sizes for an effective sample size check; all four signs persisted. Two different variance formulas matched different source groups. These are fixed-release descriptions, not sampling intervals or causal effects. Shared droughts, detection, publication selection, different metrics and incomplete dates limit inference. The extract did not support balanced independent-period tests. No air pollution effect was tested. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and source hashes are included.
